I will do it much like I did last year, with a few small changes from what I saw around me. I have farmed in Quzhou for many years, and I do not like making big changes all at once. I have well water, so I will not let the crop suffer if the rain is short. On my bigger area, I have to think about cost, but I also know that if I save too much on fertilizer and the yield drops, that loss is worse. So I will keep cotton as the main crop, because that is what fits my land and my habit, then I will keep some maize and wheat for steady grain, and some stevia where it gave decent cash before. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it has shown good performance nearby, because now most people around me do that and it is safer than old seed. For fertilizer, I will not go too low. Cotton and stevia need feeding if I want a good stand and enough picking weight, maize needs enough base fertilizer and one topdressing, and wheat must not go hungry before jointing. With water, I will rely on the well and give the more important irrigations at the key time. For pesticides, I will not spray blindly, but I know cotton needs more watching than the others. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is quicker on my area and costs less labor than deep ploughing every time. This year I will keep the plan steady, spend money first on seed, fertilizer, water, and the main sprays, and I will chase a reliable harvest instead of gambling on cutting too much cost.
